slice: Act 1 -- The Crack Under the Couch
sampleRate: 44100 Hz (music/SFX render) / 44100 Hz (voice TTS render), all exported mono OGG Vorbis

cues.purpose: Quiet, dusty room-tone bed for the entry chamber -- loops under all Act 1 gameplay.
Short goofy success sting layered with sfx/toll-gate-open.ogg when Old Bottlecap accepts the button.
Soft blip on menu/hotspot hover.
Confirmation blip when a hotspot or dialogue choice is selected.
Descending blip when backing out of a menu or dialogue.
Pip's footstep on the under-couch floor, variant 1; alternate with variant 2.
Pip's footstep, variant 2; alternate with variant 1.
Soft reveal chime when searching the dust clump uncovers the button (act01-005).
Small metallic clink when the button is actually added to inventory.
Soft cardboard creak when inspecting the Lost & Found Cubby Wall.
Page-turn when inspecting the Sign-In Log (act01-011).
Soft heavy thud on the popcorn-kernel boulder's permanent use-fail (act01-013).
Soft cloth/web rustle when inspecting the cobweb curtain, just before Scuttle's cameo.
Fast skitter under Scuttle's one-shot cameo dash-through (act01-015).
Soft dismissive knock when Old Bottlecap refuses entry without the toll (act01-038).
Grate sliding open, layered with music/toll-paid-stinger.ogg -- the act's climax beat.
Ambient paper-shuffle one-shot during Bramble's passive furniture-anchored idle loop, played periodically, not player-triggered.
Institutional bureaucratic room tone (murmur, distant office activity) for the Exchange Concourse -- loops under all Act 2 gameplay, replacing Act 1's cozier underneath-ambience-loop for this scene.
Dark, hollow storage-room tone for the Annex -- loops from the cold open through the Toggle confrontation, until roar-arrives cuts over to roar-escape-tension-loop.

Fast, percussion-driven tension loop replacing the Annex ambience once the Roar hits -- carries the whole Sec 3-5 escape sequence (Grommet's block, the dash to the Grate, the final push through), stops on roar-passed.
Warm resolution sting under the closing goodbye beat and Pip's epilogue line (act03-057/058) -- the game's single biggest emotional beat, deliberately bigger than Act 1's toll-paid-stinger.

Shared 'combine' sound language for the whole game -- plays whenever two inventory items combine into one: Act 2's needle+thread->threaded-needle (act02-023) and Act 3's founders-ledger+intake-parcel->annotated-evidence (act03-028). One sound, reused by trigger, not two near-identical assets.
Soft parcel-hits-floor thud when Scuttle fumbles the intake parcel (act02-036).

Chairman Toggle's decisive stamp-thud on petition denial (act02-067). Reused wherever else he stamps something dismissively in Act 3's deflect beats (act03-022, act03-026) -- one prop sound for the character, not a unique stamp per line.
Low, distant rumble under the light-flicker foreshadowing beat (act02-070/071) -- low-intensity version of sfx/roar-rumble.ogg, establishes the visual/audio language Act 3's roar-arrives escalates.
Heavy wooden door creak-open when Grommet lets Pip into the Annex (act03-003) -- distinct material (wood, not metal) from Act 1's toll-gate-open.

Small glass-marble handling/clink sound, shared across all 5 marble-pile candidates' take attempts (act03-010/012/014/016/018) -- both fails and the success reuse the same physical sound, only the dialogue differs.

Small comedic balloon-deflate whoosh on Chairman Toggle's concession (act03-032) -- a pun on his own name, and per docs/STORY_ARC.md's note that his defeat should read embarrassed, not crushed, this is deliberately funny, not a victory fanfare.

The Roar itself -- a real vacuum-cleaner run sound, layered under music/roar-escape-tension-loop.ogg for the full escape sequence. Faded down (not re-sourced) for the inverse roar-passed cue once Pip checks on Grommet (act03-048).
Fabric-flapping wind-rush loop under Grommet holding the chokepoint against the draft (act03-036 onward) -- the game's climax beat, sustains for however long the escape sequence's timing needs.

voiceDialogueNote: Voice lines are ElevenLabs TTS on a paid Creator-tier account -- commercial use permitted, still requires ElevenLabs attribution per their ToS. All three acts are fully voiced: 49/49 (Act 1), 72/72 (Act 2), 58/58 (Act 3). See script/ACT_0{1,2,3}_DIALOGUE.json and README.md's Voice Audio section.
